newsitem.title: USA: TENNIS-HINGIS, PIERCE REACH TOSHIBA CLASSIC SEMIFINALS.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-HINGIS, PIERCE REACH TOSHIBA CLASSIC SEMIFINALS.

text.p: World number one
Martina Hingis fought off a determined challenge from seventh
seed Conchita Martinez Friday to advance to the semifinals of
the Toshiba Tennis Classic.
Just five days after blowing out the Spaniard in a final
at Palo Alto to claim her eighth title of the year, Hingis
needed eight match points to close out a 6-4 6-4 victory.
"She hit some really good returns and she was fighting
'til the end," said Hingis after needing one hour and 42
minutes to run her 1997 record to 52-1.
"It was one of the hardest matches for me and I'm really
happy what I did out there today," added Hingis, who in the
semifinals will face sixth seed Mary Pierce in a rematch of
the Australian Open final won by Hingis.
Pierce was in excellent form in pounding out a 6-3 6-2
victory French Fed Cup teammate Sandrine Testud and was ready
for another shot at Hingis.
"I'm excited. She's playing great tennis, she's been very
tough to beat lately," Pierce said of the game's teen queen
who is 25-0 on hard courts this year. "I'm very much looking
forward to playing her."
Saturday's other semifinal pits second seed Monica Seles
against sixth-seeded South African Amanda Coetzer.
Pierce was on the mark with her aggressive ground attack
as she smacked 29 winners. She also won 16 of 18 net
approaches.
"She played too good tonight," said the 20th-ranked
Testud. "She was able to hit winners from everywhere on the
court and she served very well."
Pierce steamrolled through the second set, winning 20 of
the final 22 points.
Last Sunday, the 16-year-old Swiss sensation drubbed a
weary Martinez 6-2 6-0 in 53 minutes to win the Bank of West
title. The Spaniard was ready to make a better showing Friday.
"It was a great match. I was very rested today," said
Martinez. "I had my chances for sure. It's good I gave her a
very good match. Hopefully, next time I can beat her."
Hingis had her hands full with the 10th-ranked Spaniard's
array of topspin groundstrokes Friday.
"Conchita was much stronger this time," noted Hingis, who
managed to convert just four of 16 break opportunities. "She
knew what she had to do against me and she did it pretty
well."
Hingis claimed the opening set with a pair of service
breaks and built a 5-2 advantage in the second before Martinez
took advantage of a mental lapse by the Swiss teen.
Martinez successfully fought off three match points in the
ninth game to reach 4-5, leaving a frustrated Hingis swatting
balls into the net in anger.
"She was really hard to finish off," Hingis said. "When
you're leading 6-4, 5-2, you're already thinking it's over.
"You kind of think it's gonna end by itself but it
doesn't."
With Hingis serving for the match at 5-4, Martinez saved
four more match points before finally succumbing when she
slapped a backhand service return into the net on the eighth
match point of the contest.
